issues.legal_issue: A pleading amendment sought after trial has commenced is not permitted when the applicant could have raised the matter earlier despite having relevant knowledge and seeks materially different relief.
material_facts: The plaintiff originally sought a declaration of exclusive rights over the property.
Before filing suit, the plaintiff had been told that another company was occupying the property and conducting mining operations under a lease from the government.
The government’s written statement also described the lease and its transfer to that company.
Despite this information, the plaintiff did not seek possession or damages in the original suit and proceeded through the evidence.
After the evidence had closed and arguments were underway, the plaintiff sought to add claims for possession and damages.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff did not satisfy the requirement that the matter could not have been raised earlier despite due diligence. The amendment was also sought at a late stage and added substantive relief beyond the original claim. The High Court therefore rightly set aside the order allowing the amendment, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 17 CPC, as substituted by the Code of Civil Procedure (Amendment) Act, 2002 with effect from 1 July 2002, permits amendments necessary to determine the real questions in controversy, but an amendment after trial has commenced may be allowed only if the court is satisfied that, despite due diligence, the matter could not have been raised earlier. Pre-trial amendments are to be considered more liberally. The Court also noted that amendment may be refused where it changes the nature of the claim, introduces a new cause of action intended to prejudice the other party, or defeats limitation. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: civil_suit_amendment_request and trial_commenced and applicant_lacked_due_diligence and amendment_added_distinct_substantive_relief

predicates.civil_suit_amendment_request: A party in a civil suit sought to amend its pleading.
predicates.trial_commenced: The applicant sought the amendment after the evidence had closed and arguments were underway.
predicates.applicant_lacked_due_diligence: The applicant knew the relevant facts before trial but did not seek the amendment until arguments were underway.
predicates.amendment_added_distinct_substantive_rel: The proposed amendment added claims for possession and damages to a suit that had originally sought declaratory relief.

issues.definition: When a party in a civil suit seeks an amendment after trial has commenced, had relevant facts earlier but failed to act on them, and seeks distinct substantive relief, the amendment is disallowed.
